{{recipe}} | [[Cookbook:Bread|Bread]] | [[Cookbook:Cuisine of France|French cuisine]] | [[Cookbook:Salad|Salads]] | [[Cookbook:Soups|Soups]]

'''Garlic croutons''' can be purchased but are much better when made from old bread. They are a crucial ingredient of [[Cookbook:Caesar_Salad|Caesar Salad]].

== Ingredients ==
*4 slices day-old French bread, [[Cookbook:Cube|cubed]]
*2 cloves [[Cookbook:Garlic|garlic]], [[Cookbook:Mincing|minced]]
*4 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tablespoons]] [[Cookbook:Olive_oil|olive oil]]
*[[Cookbook:Salt|Salt]] to taste

== Procedure ==
# Pour the olive oil into a shallow bowl over the garlic and let it soak. Soaking it longer will yield more garlic flavor.
# Preheat the [[Cookbook:Oven|oven]] to 350 °F (~180 °C).
# [[Cookbook:Straining|Strain]] the olive oil into a [[Cookbook:Frying Pan|frying pan]] and [[Cookbook:Frying|fry]] the bread cubes in it, [[Cookbook:Mixing#Tossing|tossing]] to coat with oil.
# Spread the bread cubes on a [[Cookbook:Baking Sheet|baking sheet]] and sprinkle with salt. [[Cookbook:Baking|Bake]] for 10 minutes or until crispy and dry.

== Notes, tips, and variations ==
* To make non-garlic croutons, simply omit the garlic.
* One may omit the prep work of mincing the garlic by adding the whole cloves of garlic to the oil and then crushing the garlic (either with a mortar or a fork).
* By using very small bread cubes, frying crisp, and omitting the baking, these croutons may be used in place of potatoes.
